In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: 1) the design of the dual-core HOG feature extraction accelerator, which is a key component of a pedestrian detection system; 2) the implementation of a dual-core HOG processor with a reconfigurability of detection-window-size; 3) the design and implementation of a HOG feature extraction processor with early classification; and 4) the demonstration of a pedestrian detection application.
the design of a HOG accelerator for multiple object detection.
the design of a HOG-based real-time object detection accelerator that can process high resolution videos with low power consumption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed architecture can achieve 100% accuracy in real-time pedestrian detection.
the proposed accelerator is a highly efficient HOG feature extractor for real-time multiple shape object detection.
the HOG algorithm is a very good algorithm for object detection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a HOG feature extraction accelerator for multiple object detection in real-time applications.

this is the first HOG accelerator with the following features: a) it can be configured for high-speed mode, multiple objects detection mode or multiple shape object detection, b) it has dual cores and a reconfigurable architecture for scalable window size, c) it can operate at 100 mW, d) it has an early classification scheme for SVM classification.
we developed a real-time pedestrian detection system that operates at 30 fps with 0.5% false alarm rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HOG accelerator is a good example of how to design a high-performance and low-power VLSI processor for real-time multiple objects detection.
the proposed architecture is scalable and can be extended to process other types of objects and to support other applications.
the HOG accelerator is capable of processing HDTV resolution video with a power consumption of 98 mW, which is 1.7× lower than that of a state-of-the-art accelerator.
